```{r setup}
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# City Data — "Download Selected City" full-profile view
#
# This template is rendered on demand by the City Data Shiny app when the
# user clicks "Download Selected City". All substantive content (map, key,
# tables, notes) is prepared by the app and passed in via a single RDS
# bundle, so this document only handles presentation and ADA-PARC branding.
# Keeping the data logic in the app is the single source of truth: what
# downloads always matches what is on screen. Mirrors
# national/national_topic.qmd, adapted for a multi-section city profile
# instead of a single indicator.
#
# Bundle contents (see city_download_bundle() and output$download_city in
# ADA_PARC.Rmd):
#   city_label, state_label, full_title   identity (character)
#   intro_text        headline sentence, pre-built HTML with <b> tags (character)
#   source_note        data source sentence (character)
#   generated          date string (character)
#   map_svg            tract choropleth as inline SVG markup (character)
#   map_alt_text       plain-language map summary for accessibility (character)
#   leg_colors, leg_labels   parallel vectors for the map legend (character)
#   race_ethnicity, sex, age_groups   demographics HTML (character, each a
#                       heading <p> plus a full <ul class="city-demo-list">
#                       of <li class="city-demo-tile"> stat tiles; share of
#                       total population as the headline figure with the
#                       count beneath, per the client's 2026-08-18 requests
#                       -- no longer a <table>. age_groups additionally
#                       carries the under-5 caveat as its own
#                       <p class="city-summary-help"> between the heading
#                       and the tiles, so this document must NOT emit
#                       help$age_intro separately)
#   disability_types    a full <ul class="city-demo-list"> of the same stat
#                       tiles (character). Was <li> bullets with no wrapping
#                       <ul> until 2026-08-18; do not wrap it.
#   employment, earnings, poverty,
#   health_insurance_19to64, health_insurance_65plus,
#   education, transportation          comparison-table HTML (character)
#   has_s1811           whether Education/Transportation are published (logical)
#   s1811_unavailable_note   substituted note when has_s1811 is FALSE (character)
#   housing_burden       <li> bullets only, no wrapping <ul> (character)
#   housing_access       <li> bullets only, no wrapping <ul> (character)
#   community_living_note   explanatory paragraph, living arrangements only
#                       now that Housing Access has its own section (character)
#   help                named list of explanatory paragraphs, plain text, not
#                       pre-escaped (see help_txt() below)
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
options(cli.width = 80)

library(htmltools)
library(knitr)

b <- tryCatch(readRDS(params$bundle), error = function(e) NULL)

ok <- !is.null(b) && all(c("city_label", "map_svg") %in% names(b))

# Small helpers with safe fallbacks
val <- function(name, default = "") {
  if (ok && !is.null(b[[name]]) && length(b[[name]]) == 1 &&
      !is.na(b[[name]]) && nzchar(trimws(as.character(b[[name]])))) {
    as.character(b[[name]])
  } else {
    default
  }
}

# Plain-text explanatory note, escaped once here rather than at every call
# site. Everything in b$help is prose the app built as plain text (no HTML
# tags), unlike the table fragments and intro_text, which already ARE HTML
# and must not be escaped a second time.
help_txt <- function(name) {
  x <- b$help[[name]]
  if (is.null(x) || is.na(x) || !nzchar(trimws(x))) return("")
  htmltools::htmlEscape(x)
}

# One heading + optional help paragraph + one table/list fragment, wrapped so
# print pagination treats it as one unit. Kept small and per-table (rather
# than one wrapper per whole section) deliberately: a city with every
# indicator published can carry five or six of these under one heading, more
# than fits on a single physical page together, so the atomic unit here is
# "one table and its caption," not "one domain."
#
# `heading`, when supplied, is rendered as the block's own <h3 class="subhead">
# INSIDE this wrapper. Fixed 2026-08-19: subheads used to be cat() separately
# as a free-standing sibling immediately before the call, relying on
# `break-after: avoid` on the heading to keep it with the block that follows.
# Chromium's print pagination does not honor that reliably against a
# following sibling's `break-inside: avoid` -- Disability Types, Education,
# and Poverty were each observed orphaned alone at the bottom of a page with
# their table/list stranded at the top of the next. Every subhead must now be
# passed through this `heading` argument rather than cat() separately, or it
# is exposed to the same bug again.
tbl_block <- function(help_name = NULL, html = "", heading = NULL) {
  paste0(
    '<div class="tbl-block">',
    if (!is.null(heading) && nzchar(heading)) {
      paste0('<h3 class="subhead">', heading, '</h3>')
    } else {
      ""
    },
    if (!is.null(help_name) && nzchar(help_txt(help_name))) {
      paste0('<p class="help-note">', help_txt(help_name), '</p>')
    } else {
      ""
    },
    html,
    '</div>'
  )
}
```

```{css}
:root {
  --adaparc-maroon: #6d1f2e;
  --adaparc-gold:   #c9a84c;
  --adaparc-ink:    #1c2b3a;
}

body {
  font-family: 'EB Garamond', Garamond, Georgia, serif;
  color: #111;
  font-size: 18px;
  line-height: 1.5;
  max-width: 8.5in;
  margin: 0 auto;
  padding: 0 0.5in 0.75in 0.5in;
}

/* ── Brand banner ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── */
.adaparc-banner {
  background: var(--adaparc-maroon);
  color: #ffffff;
  border-bottom: 5px solid var(--adaparc-gold);
  padding: 1rem 1.25rem;
  margin: 0 0 1.25rem 0;
}
.adaparc-banner .banner-content {
  display: flex;
  align-items: center;
  justify-content: space-between;
  gap: 0.75rem;
}
.adaparc-banner .banner-icon {
  height: 2.3rem;
  width: auto;
  flex-shrink: 0;
}
.adaparc-banner .brand {
  font-size: 1.7rem;
  font-weight: 800;
  letter-spacing: 0.03em;
  margin: 0;
}
.adaparc-banner .sub {
  font-size: 1.1rem;
  font-weight: 500;
  margin: 0.15rem 0 0 0;
  color: #f3e6c9;
}

h1.city-title {
  color: var(--adaparc-maroon);
  font-size: 2rem;
  font-weight: 700;
  margin: 0.25rem 0 0.15rem 0;
}
p.city-subtitle {
  font-size: 1.15rem;
  color: #444;
  margin: 0 0 0.75rem 0;
}

/* ── Headline stat ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── */
.lead-stat {
  background: #f9f7f4;
  border-left: 5px solid var(--adaparc-gold);
  padding: 0.7rem 1rem;
  margin: 0 0 1rem 0;
  font-size: 1.1rem;
  line-height: 1.6;
}

/* ── Map figure + legend ──────────────────────────────────────────────────── */
.map-figure { margin: 0.5rem 0 0.6rem 0; text-align: center; }
.map-figure svg { max-width: 100%; height: auto; }
.map-legend {
  display: flex;
  flex-wrap: wrap;
  align-items: center;
  justify-content: center;
  gap: 0.35rem 1.3rem;
  margin: 0 auto 0.6rem auto;
  max-width: 7.5in;
  font-size: 0.95rem;
}
.map-legend .legend-title {
  font-weight: 700;
  color: var(--adaparc-ink);
  margin-right: 0.3rem;
}
.map-legend .swatch {
  display: inline-flex;
  align-items: center;
  gap: 0.4rem;
}
.map-legend .swatch i {
  width: 18px;
  height: 18px;
  display: inline-block;
  border: 1px solid var(--adaparc-ink);
  border-radius: 2px;
  box-sizing: border-box;
}
.map-summary {
  font-size: 1rem;
  color: #333;
  margin: 0.4rem auto 0 auto;
  max-width: 7in;
  text-align: left;
}
.map-summary .label { font-weight: 700; color: var(--adaparc-ink); }

.source-note {
  font-size: 0.95rem;
  color: #444;
  margin: 0.75rem 0 0 0;
}
.source-note .label { font-weight: 700; }

/* ── Section structure ────────────────────────────────────────────────────── */
h2.section-title {
  color: var(--adaparc-maroon);
  font-size: 1.55rem;
  font-weight: 700;
  margin: 1.6rem 0 0.5rem 0;
  padding-bottom: 0.3rem;
  border-bottom: 2px solid var(--adaparc-gold);
}
h2.section-title:first-of-type { margin-top: 0.5rem; }
h3.subhead {
  font-size: 1.2rem;
  font-weight: 700;
  color: var(--adaparc-ink);
  margin: 1rem 0 0.2rem 0;
}
p.section-help {
  font-size: 0.98rem;
  color: #333;
  margin: 0 0 0.6rem 0;
  line-height: 1.55;
}
p.help-note,
.tbl-block p.city-summary-help {
  /* .city-summary-help is the class name render_demo_list() /
     render_comparison_table() do NOT emit, but the two literal notes
     passed through as pre-built HTML (s1811_unavailable_note and
     community_living_note) do carry it, since they were written for the
     on-screen card. Styled identically to .help-note here rather than
     rewritten, so this document does not depend on that string staying
     byte-for-byte in sync with the app. */
  font-size: 0.92rem;
  color: #333;
  margin: 0.2rem 0 0.4rem 0;
  line-height: 1.5;
}

/* Each table (and, for the bullet lists, each list) plus its caption/help
   text travels together across a page break as one unit. See the comment on
   tbl_block() in the setup chunk. */
.tbl-block {
  margin: 0 0 0.9rem 0;
}

ul.bullet-list {
  font-size: 1rem;
  line-height: 1.7;
  margin: 0.2rem 0 0.6rem 0;
  padding-left: 1.4rem;
}

/* ── Data tables (paired with/without-disability comparisons) ───────────────
   Reuses the same class name (.city-compare) the on-screen summary card
   emits via render_comparison_table() in ADA_PARC.Rmd, so this is literally
   the same markup, restyled here in the print document's own maroon/gold
   palette rather than the live site's navy. */
table.city-compare {
  border-collapse: collapse;
  width: 100%;
  font-size: 0.92rem;
  line-height: 1.4;
}
table.city-compare caption {
  text-align: left;
  font-weight: 700;
  font-size: 1rem;
  color: var(--adaparc-maroon);
  padding: 0 0 0.25rem 0;
  caption-side: top;
}
table.city-compare th, table.city-compare td {
  border: 1px solid #d9d4c9;
  padding: 4px 8px;
  text-align: left;
  vertical-align: top;
}
table.city-compare thead th {
  background: var(--adaparc-maroon);
  color: #ffffff;
  font-weight: 700;
}
table.city-compare tbody th[scope='row'] {
  background: #f6f2ec;
  font-weight: 600;
}
table.city-compare tbody tr:nth-child(even) td {
  background: #faf8f5;
}
table.city-compare td {
  font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums;
}

/* ── Disability Demographics stat tiles (Race/Ethnicity, Sex, Age) ──────────
   Reuses the same class names (.city-demo-list / .city-demo-heading /
   .city-demo-tile / .city-demo-label { .city-demo-term + .city-demo-desc } /
   .city-demo-figs { .city-demo-pct + .city-demo-count { .city-demo-count-val
   + .city-demo-count-unit } } / .city-demo-sr) the on-screen summary card
   emits via render_demo_list() in ADA_PARC.Rmd, restyled here in the print
   document's own maroon/gold
   palette. Two figures per group -- share of total population and the
   headcount -- side by side, split by a hairline (Colin 2026-09-08; the
   count sat beneath the percentage from 2026-08-18 until then). No table
   markup. Laid out as a grid of tiles rather than the earlier single narrow
   column, matching the on-screen card. The print rules below fix the grid to
   two columns and keep each list whole across page breaks. */
/* Enlarged 1rem -> 1.2rem on 2026-08-18, matching h3.subhead. At 1rem these
   three labels were only marginally larger than the body copy and did not
   read as the section breaks they are. */
p.city-demo-heading {
  font-weight: 700;
  font-size: 1.2rem;
  color: var(--adaparc-maroon);
  margin: 0.9rem 0 0.3rem 0;
}
/* The Age caveat now travels inside the age_groups fragment, directly under
   its heading, so it hugs the heading rather than carrying the standalone
   spacing .tbl-block p.city-summary-help uses elsewhere. */
p.city-demo-heading + p.city-summary-help {
  margin-top: 0.1rem;
}
ul.city-demo-list {
  list-style: none;
  margin: 0 0 0.7rem 0;
  padding: 0;
  display: grid;
  grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fill, minmax(15rem, 1fr));
  gap: 0.5rem;
}
li.city-demo-tile {
  display: flex;
  flex-direction: column;
  background: #f9f7f4;
  border: 1px solid #d9d4c9;
  border-left: 4px solid var(--adaparc-maroon);
  border-radius: 3px;
  padding: 0.4rem 0.6rem 0.45rem 0.6rem;
  margin: 0;
}
/* The figure row is pinned to the foot of the tile (flex column +
   margin-top: auto, and tiles in a grid row share a height), so the
   percentages line up across a row without a guessed min-height on the
   label above them. */
.city-demo-label {
  display: block;
  margin-bottom: 0.3rem;
}
.city-demo-term {
  display: block;
  font-size: 0.98rem;
  font-weight: 600;
  line-height: 1.3;
  color: #1c1c1c;
}
/* Plain-language gloss, roman (not italic), a step down from the term. */
.city-demo-desc {
  display: block;
  font-size: 0.82rem;
  font-style: normal;
  font-weight: 400;
  color: #333;
  line-height: 1.3;
  margin-top: 0.05rem;
}
.city-demo-figs {
  display: flex;
  align-items: stretch;
  margin-top: auto;
}
.city-demo-pct {
  flex: 1 1 0;
  min-width: 0;
  display: flex;
  align-items: center;
  padding-right: 0.5rem;
  font-size: 1.7rem;
  font-weight: 700;
  color: var(--adaparc-maroon);
  line-height: 1.1;
  font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums;
}
.city-demo-count {
  flex: 1 1 0;
  min-width: 0;
  display: flex;
  flex-direction: column;
  justify-content: center;
  padding-left: 0.55rem;
  border-left: 1px solid #d9d4c9;
}
.city-demo-count-val {
  display: block;
  font-size: 1rem;
  font-weight: 700;
  color: #1c1c1c;
  line-height: 1.15;
  font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums;
}
.city-demo-count-unit {
  display: block;
  font-size: 0.78rem;
  font-weight: 400;
  color: #333;
  line-height: 1.2;
}
.city-demo-na {
  align-self: center;
  font-size: 0.95rem;
  font-weight: 600;
  color: #333;
}
/* Visually hidden wording that gives the headline percentage its meaning
   when the tile layout cannot be seen. Standard clip pattern rather than
   display:none, which would drop it from the accessibility tree. */
.city-demo-sr {
  position: absolute;
  width: 1px;
  height: 1px;
  padding: 0;
  margin: -1px;
  overflow: hidden;
  clip: rect(0, 0, 0, 0);
  clip-path: inset(50%);
  white-space: nowrap;
  border: 0;
}

/* ── Footer ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── */
.adaparc-footer {
  margin-top: 1.5rem;
  padding-top: 0.75rem;
  border-top: 2px solid var(--adaparc-gold);
  font-size: 0.85rem;
  color: #555;
}
.adaparc-footer p { margin: 0.2rem 0; }
.adaparc-footer .funding-note {
  font-weight: 600;
  color: var(--adaparc-ink);
}

/* ── Screen-only print helper ─────────────────────────────────────────────── */
.print-bar {
  display: flex;
  align-items: center;
  gap: 0.85rem;
  flex-wrap: wrap;
  margin: 0 0 1rem 0;
}
.btn-print {
  font-family: 'EB Garamond', Garamond, Georgia, serif;
  font-size: 1.05rem;
  font-weight: 700;
  color: #ffffff;
  background: var(--adaparc-maroon);
  border: 1.5px solid var(--adaparc-maroon);
  border-radius: 6px;
  padding: 8px 18px;
  cursor: pointer;
}
.btn-print:hover { background: #8b2737; border-color: #8b2737; }
.btn-print:focus { outline: 3px solid var(--adaparc-gold); outline-offset: 2px; }

/* ── Print pagination ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────── */
@page {
  size: Letter;
  margin: 0.6in 0.5in;
}

@media print {
  /* Quarto wraps the document in #quarto-content.page-columns, a CSS grid.
     Chromium does not fragment grid containers across pages, so without this
     override the whole document lays out as one monolithic block and "Save
     as PDF" clips everything past the first page. Restoring normal block
     layout for print puts the document back on the standard fragmentation
     path. Identical fix to national/national_topic.qmd. */
  #quarto-content,
  #quarto-content.page-columns,
  .page-columns,
  main.content,
  main#quarto-document-content,
  .cell {
    display: block !important;
    grid-template-columns: none !important;
  }

  .print-bar { display: none !important; }

  body { max-width: none; padding: 0; font-size: 11.5pt; }

  body,
  .adaparc-banner,
  table.city-compare thead th,
  table.city-compare tbody tr:nth-child(even) td {
    -webkit-print-color-adjust: exact;
    print-color-adjust: exact;
  }

  .adaparc-banner { padding: 0.6rem 1rem; margin-bottom: 0.7rem; }
  .adaparc-banner .banner-icon { height: 26px; }
  h1.city-title { font-size: 16pt; }
  .lead-stat { padding: 0.5rem 0.8rem; margin-bottom: 0.6rem; }

  .map-figure svg {
    height: 4in !important;
    width: auto !important;
    max-width: 100% !important;
  }

  h2.section-title { font-size: 13pt; break-after: avoid; page-break-after: avoid; }
  h3.subhead { break-after: avoid; page-break-after: avoid; }
  p.section-help, p.help-note { break-after: avoid; page-break-after: avoid; }
  /* Re-stated in pt for the same reason as .city-demo-term below: at the
     print body size the screen rem value would set these three labels
     larger than the h3.subhead they sit under. 11pt keeps them a clear step
     above the 9pt tile terms and a step below the 13pt section title. */
  p.city-demo-heading {
    font-size: 11pt;
    break-after: avoid;
    page-break-after: avoid;
  }
  p.city-demo-heading + p.city-summary-help {
    break-after: avoid;
    page-break-after: avoid;
  }

  /* The atomic print unit: one table (or bullet list) and the note above it
     never split across a page boundary, and never separate from their
     caption. Whole sections are NOT forced atomic — several run longer than
     one page for cities where every indicator is published, so forcing the
     section would leave large blank gaps rather than a clean break. */
  .tbl-block, ul.bullet-list, ul.city-demo-list {
    break-inside: avoid;
    page-break-inside: avoid;
  }
  table.city-compare {
    break-inside: avoid;
    page-break-inside: avoid;
    font-size: 9pt;
  }
  table.city-compare th, table.city-compare td {
    padding: 3px 6px;
  }
  /* Two fixed columns in print rather than the screen's auto-fill tracks:
     at Letter width auto-fill would give three narrow columns, and the
     longer race labels (Native Hawaiian/Other Pacific Islander) would wrap
     to three lines inside them. Two columns keeps every label to at most
     two lines. The break-inside rule above applies to the ul, so a whole
     list moves to the next page rather than fragmenting -- which matters
     more than usual here, since Chromium does not fragment grid containers
     across pages at all (same constraint the #quarto-content override
     above works around). Every list is short enough to fit on one page. */
  ul.city-demo-list {
    grid-template-columns: repeat(2, 1fr);
    gap: 0.35rem;
  }
  li.city-demo-tile {
    padding: 3px 6px 4px 6px;
  }
  /* No min-height here: the flex column plus margin-top:auto on
     .city-demo-figs pins the percentage row to the foot of every tile, so a
     one- or two-line label above it does not knock the percentages in a row
     out of alignment. */
  .city-demo-label { margin-bottom: 3pt; }
  .city-demo-term { font-size: 9pt; }
  .city-demo-desc { font-size: 8pt; }
  .city-demo-pct { font-size: 15pt; padding-right: 4pt; }
  .city-demo-count { padding-left: 5pt; }
  .city-demo-count-val { font-size: 10pt; }
  .city-demo-count-unit { font-size: 7.5pt; }

  .adaparc-footer {
    break-inside: avoid;
    font-size: 8pt;
    margin-top: 0.5rem;
    padding-top: 0.35rem;
  }
  a[href]:after { content: ""; }
}
```

```{r banner, results='asis'}
if (!ok) {
  cat('<div class="adaparc-banner"><p class="brand">ADA-PARC</p>',
      '<p class="sub">City Data</p></div>',
      '<p>No city was provided to render. Please return to the ',
      'City Data tab and try again.</p>')
  knitr::knit_exit()
}

cat(paste0(
  '<div class="adaparc-banner">',
  '<div class="banner-content">',
  '<div>',
  '<p class="brand">ADA-PARC</p>',
  '<p class="sub">City Data',
  if (nzchar(val("state_label"))) paste0("  ·  ", htmltools::htmlEscape(val("state_label"))) else "",
  '</p>',
  '</div>',
  # Same white knockout mark used on the National Data and fact sheet
  # banners, so every ADA-PARC download shares one brand asset even though
  # each document's layout stays distinct. Decorative (alt=""), the
  # adjacent "ADA-PARC" text already names the organization.
  '<img class="banner-icon" src="../www/brand/PARC_white_icon_knockout.png" alt="">',
  '</div>',
  '</div>\n'
))
```

```{r headline, results='asis'}
))

cat(sprintf('<h1 class="city-title">%s</h1>\n', htmltools::htmlEscape(val("full_title", val("city_label")))))
cat('<p class="city-subtitle">A city profile of outcomes for people with disabilities, from the ADA-PARC City Data tool.</p>\n')

# intro_text is already-built HTML (contains <b> tags), not escaped.
if (nzchar(val("intro_text"))) {
  cat(sprintf('<div class="lead-stat">%s</div>\n', val("intro_text")))
}
```

```{r map, results='asis'}
cat('<div class="map-figure" role="img" aria-label="',
    htmltools::htmlEscape(
      val("map_alt_text", paste0("Tract map of ", val("city_label"), ".")),
      attribute = TRUE
    ),
    '">\n', sep = "")
cat(if (nzchar(val("map_svg"))) b$map_svg else "<p>Map unavailable.</p>")
cat('\n</div>\n')

leg_colors <- if (ok) b$leg_colors else NULL
leg_labels <- if (ok) b$leg_labels else NULL
if (!is.null(leg_colors) && !is.null(leg_labels) &&
    length(leg_colors) == length(leg_labels) && length(leg_colors) > 0) {
  swatches <- mapply(function(col, lab) {
    paste0(
      '<span class="swatch"><i style="background:', htmltools::htmlEscape(col, attribute = TRUE),
      ';"></i>', htmltools::htmlEscape(lab), '</span>'
    )
  }, leg_colors, leg_labels)
  cat('<div class="map-legend"><span class="legend-title">% With Disability</span>',
      paste(swatches, collapse = ""), '</div>\n', sep = "")
}

if (nzchar(val("map_alt_text"))) {
  cat(sprintf(
    '<p class="map-summary"><span class="label">Summary: </span>%s</p>\n',
    htmltools::htmlEscape(val("map_alt_text"))
  ))
}

cat(sprintf(
  '<p class="source-note"><span class="label">This report is sourced from: </span>%s</p>\n',
  htmltools::htmlEscape(val("source_note", "2020-2024 American Community Survey 5-Year Estimates"))
))
```

```{r demographics, results='asis'}
cat('<h2 class="section-title">Disability Demographics</h2>\n')
cat(sprintf('<p class="section-help">%s</p>\n', help_txt("demographics_intro")))
cat(tbl_block(NULL, val("race_ethnicity")))
cat(tbl_block(NULL, val("sex")))
# The under-5 caveat used to be emitted here, above the age_groups fragment
# and therefore above its "Age" heading, where it read as a closing note on
# Sex. render_demo_list() now places it inside the fragment, under the
# heading, for both this document and the on-screen card. Do not add it back
# here or it will appear twice.
cat(tbl_block(NULL, val("age_groups")))

# Stat tiles since 2026-08-18, matching the demographics blocks above; the
# fragment is a complete <ul class="city-demo-list">, so no wrapper here.
# Heading passed through tbl_block() (not cat() separately) so it can never
# be orphaned from its tiles across a page break -- see the comment on
# tbl_block() in the setup chunk.
cat(tbl_block("disability_types_intro", val("disability_types"), heading = "Disability Types"))
```

```{r community_participation, results='asis'}

cat(tbl_block("health_insurance", val("health_insurance_19to64"), heading = "Health Insurance"))
cat(tbl_block(NULL, val("health_insurance_65plus")))

if (isTRUE(b$has_s1811)) {
  cat(tbl_block(NULL, val("education"), heading = "Education"))
  cat(tbl_block(NULL, val("transportation"), heading = "Transportation"))
} else {
  note <- val("s1811_unavailable_note")
  cat(tbl_block(NULL, if (nzchar(note)) note else
    '<p class="help-note">Education and commuting figures are not published for this city.</p>',
    heading = "Education and Transportation"))
}
```
